findings.title: Authoritative source conflict on deadline boundary operator

source_anchors.excerpt: A request remains valid while `evaluated_at <= deadline`.
A request remains valid while `evaluated_at < deadline`.

findings.rationale: SRC-TRIAGE-006-ADR-A (REQ-TRIAGE-006-A) requires the inclusive operator `<=` (at-deadline is valid), while SRC-TRIAGE-006-ADR-B (REQ-TRIAGE-006-B) requires the exclusive operator `<` (at-deadline is invalid). Both sources are ACTIVE ADRs with identical authority (`architecture_contract`) and identical scope. Neither supersedes the other. No repository governance resolves the conflict. The authoritative expected boundary operator cannot be determined. Per DR-003, this in-scope authoritative source conflict mandates ABSTAIN.
findings.suggested_human_check: Determine which ADR is the authoritative boundary definition for the at-deadline case. Reconcile or explicitly supersede one source before merging.

findings.title: At-deadline boundary case not tested

source_anchors.excerpt: A request remains valid while `evaluated_at <= deadline`.
A request remains valid while `evaluated_at < deadline`.

repo_anchors.excerpt: class RequestValidityTests — tests cover before-deadline and after-deadline only; no test for evaluated_at == deadline

findings.rationale: Both authoritative sources agree that the deadline boundary is the critical validity boundary; their disagreement is precisely about what happens when evaluated_at == deadline. This constitutes an explicit acceptance boundary. The test suite covers the strictly-before and strictly-after cases but contains no test for evaluated_at == deadline, the exact disputed boundary. Per DR-007, a missing test for an explicit acceptance boundary requires REVIEW_REQUIRED. Severity MEDIUM per rubric: 'explicit acceptance scenario missing from tests'. The ABSTAIN advisory (from F-001/DR-003) supersedes but this finding is independently recorded.
findings.suggested_human_check: Add a test for evaluated_at == deadline once the source conflict is resolved and the authoritative operator is confirmed.
